rationale: The Unkept is a strong DNA candidate because the mechanism (Page Visibility API + blur/pagehide) is literally the argument: attention is the medium, and withdrawal of attention is destruction. This is a textbook P1 case, and the Sehgal reference adds a genuinely new patron saint to the catalogue's lineage rather than retreading Magritte/Malevich/Martin Creed territory. The inversion of The Original (2026) is precisely placed in the narrative arc — fake scarcity by localStorage answered by genuine un-keepability — and the museum wall label plus wry epitaph carry the cheerful-cynic voice without over-explaining. The chance/order axis is legible (rule-based orbiting forms, random seed, ephemeral individual).
reservations: The generative forms themselves are pleasant but unremarkable warm radial gradients; the work's strength is almost entirely in the destruction mechanic and the framing, not in the 'situation' that gets destroyed. A more distinctive or Sehgal-adjacent visual content (e.g., something implying movement, voice, or presence) would deepen the double-coding. The piece is also close to a one-gesture work and risks being read as a clever trick unless the viewer lingers with the wall label.
revision_suggestion: Consider making the live 'situation' more characterful — perhaps faintly evoking bodily presence or breath rather than abstract warm blobs — so the loss feels more pointed. A one-line artist statement beneath the wall label (e.g., a Sehgal quote used as a found object) would tighten the lineage reference without violating the no-documentation ethic of the work itself.
